title: Motion of a Freely Falling Body
topicTitle: Motion of a freely falling body
notes: **Freely falling body:** an object dropped from rest with no air resistance, falling solely under gravity.
**Acceleration is $g$ downward:** the equations of motion simplify because $a = g$ and initial velocity $u = 0$.
**Upward motion:** when a body is thrown upward, gravity acts downward. The equations become $v = u - gt$, $h = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$, $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$.
**Time to reach maximum height:** at the top, $v = 0$, so $t_{up} = u/g$. The total time of flight for a body thrown up and caught at the same level is $T = 2u/g$.
**Maximum height:** $H = u^2/(2g)$. A larger $u$ gives a much larger $H$ because height scales with the square of the initial speed.
